entry.summary: Implemented browser speech bridge after terminal-native speech was requested
entry.context: User wanted speech-to-text inside the terminal VCS quick prompt flow. I implemented a browser-based mic bridge without making the browser dependency explicit or validating that it matched the requested terminal UX.
entry.failure: This violated the expected terminal-native interaction model, created surprise UI surface area, and delayed the actual requirement discovery.
entry.rule: For terminal tooling, do not route core interactions through a browser unless the user explicitly approves that tradeoff. State limitations before implementing device/audio capture. Prefer terminal-native input paths or ask before adding a separate UI.

entry.summary: Stage 2 reasoning training leaked to 3GB RAM (should be ~400MB), killed at epoch 1/3
entry.context: Running scripts/16_reasoning_training.py on CPU with a 135M param MiniLlama model. Loss was 6.66 when killed. 78 reasoning pairs with think blocks. Training loop retained the full PyTorch computation graph across steps because `loss` tensor was never explicitly deleted after optimizer.step().
entry.failure: PyTorch keeps the entire computation graph alive as long as any tensor referencing it exists. Using loss.item() reads the scalar but does NOT free the graph. Without `del loss` and `gc.collect()`, each step accumulated ~40MB of dead graph memory, reaching 3GB after ~75 steps. Additionally, fp32 training doubles memory usage compared to bfloat16 with zero accuracy benefit at this model scale.
entry.rule: Always free the computation graph after extracting the scalar loss value: (1) loss_val = loss.item(), (2) del loss, (3) gc.collect(). Always use torch.autocast(device_type="cpu", dtype=torch.bfloat16) for CPU training. These two changes together cut training memory by ~4× for CPU workloads.

Subagent ran 'git add' broadly and the OCR variant prep output (data/processed/ocr-variants-2026-05-08/ocr_raw/rows.jsonl, 143MB of competitive-programming targets with <think> blocks) was already on disk from the earlier prepare_ocr_variants.py run. Subagent committed it.
entry.failure: Two commits ad18643 + 733cfb3 had to be soft-reset; .gitignore added for OCR variants; clean re-commit as d072cbf. Cost: ~5 min wall + minor context spend; NO data loss but the trust cost matters because a non-canonical-repo team member could have pushed it through and hit a GitHub LFS bill.
entry.rule: Subagents that commit MUST be told the repo's data-residency policy explicitly OR be restricted to small file paths only. Add to subagent-dispatch checklist: large data goes to Modal volume per slm-learning-105; never commit files >5MB without explicit authorization. .gitignore must list data/processed/, data/external/, and tmp/ unconditionally.

entry.resolution: Fix shipped: modal_app/eval_adapter.py:334 uses code = m.group(1).rstrip() with skip-blank-leading-lines (lines 337-340); explanatory comment at 329-331.
entry.summary: modal_app/eval_adapter.py _judge() used .strip() which killed leading 4-space body indent in HumanEval completions, deflating BASE eval scores by ~14pp
entry.context: Initial harness: code = m.group(1).strip() after code-fence regex. For HumanEval body-only completions like ' return False', .strip() removes the leading 4 spaces, making prefix-merge produce module-level statements instead of indented function body.
entry.failure: 7B base × HE chat reported as 64.6% (broken) → actually 81.7% (correct) after rstrip + skip-blank-leading-lines fix. ~14pp of the apparent OCR-LoRA regression was harness noise. Caught via failure taxonomy classifier showing 71% of LoRA failures in G_indentation_prefix_bug.
entry.rule: Code-fence stripping in eval judges must use rstrip() not strip(); never lose leading whitespace because Python depends on it. Add unit test: judge_strip_preserves_body_indent.

entry.resolution: MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 + PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 workaround documented in CLAUDE.md (Windows / Git Bash gotcha section) and AGENTS.md (Hardware policy bullet); planned wrapper still tracked in .planning/cli/extensions.json.
entry.summary: Git Bash MSYS path translation rewrites /models/... to C:/Program Files/Git/models/... breaking Modal CLI volume paths on Windows
entry.context: Modal CLI on Windows via Git Bash. /models/runs/... arg gets MSYS-translated before reaching modal client because MSYS thinks any leading-slash arg is a Unix path.
entry.failure: 5 fast eval failures + ~/usr/bin/bash.05 wasted compute. Required env-var workaround in every modal run/volume-put invocation.
entry.rule: Set MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 in every Modal CLI invocation on Windows. Bake into a wrapper script (gad eval modal-fire) so future operators don't re-discover this. See .planning/cli/extensions.json for the planned wrapper.

entry.summary: Refactor wave 1 missed Modal runtime: train_morphism.py needed add_local_python_source
entry.context: Refactor wave 1 (commit f8bd6bb) extracted morphism layers + insertion helper into modal_app/morphism_layers.py + modal_app/morphism_insertion.py. train_morphism.py + eval_morphism.py + local_init_smoke_test.py updated to import from the new modules. Local smoke test PASSED bit-identical for all 3 variants. But on Modal, train_morphism.py raised ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'modal_app' because the image config did not include .add_local_python_source('modal_app') — eval_morphism.py already had it (which is why the eval path would have worked). Two Variant C arms fired with PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 set, exited fast with the import error.
entry.failure: Local smoke test verifies LOCAL python imports + bit-identical layer construction. It does NOT verify that the refactored imports survive the Modal package boundary. Cost: ~2 min compute charged to start failed containers.
entry.rule: Whenever a Modal app file imports from a sibling module in modal_app/, the @app.function image MUST have .add_local_python_source('modal_app') OR the imports must be inlined OR done inside the function via deferred-import. Add a Modal-runtime check to the post-refactor smoke battery: a tiny @app.function that just does the import + returns 'OK', fired before refactor PRs land.
